artigo.texto: Resumo - Nscale negocia vender capacidade à Anthropic em acordo de até US$ 45 bilhões - Seria o segundo grande contrato entre as duas empresas no complexo Monarch - Novo prédio teria 460 MW e usaria chips Vera Rubin, da Nvidia - Acordos já firmados entre as empresas somam até US$ 44,6 bilhões A Anthropic, responsável pelo chatbot Claude, negocia com a Nscale um contrato de infraestrutura de inteligência artificial (IA) que pode alcançar US$ 45 bilhões. A informação é de pessoas próximas às negociações. A Nscale, empresa de computação em nuvem apoiada pela Nvidia, pretende fechar um novo acordo para ampliar sua operação nos Estados Unidos. Dessa vez, o contrato envolve uma segunda instalação no complexo de data centers Monarch, na Virgínia Ocidental. As duas companhias já mantêm contratos de infraestrutura que somam aproximadamente US$ 44,6 bilhões. Os valores aparecem em documentos regulatórios relacionados à oferta pública inicial de ações (IPO) da Nscale. Novo prédio terá chips Vera Rubin da Nvidia O novo edifício do complexo Monarch poderá oferecer 460 megawatts de capacidade computacional. Para sustentar a operação, a Nscale pretende utilizar chips de inteligência artificial Vera Rubin, desenvolvidos pela Nvidia. Além disso, a Anthropic poderá obter preferência na contratação de um terceiro prédio que a Nscale planeja construir no mesmo campus. Segundo fontes ouvidas sob anonimato, as empresas podem concluir o acordo nos próximos dias. No entanto, as negociações continuam e ainda podem sofrer alterações. Procuradas, Anthropic e Nscale não comentaram o assunto. Quando estiver totalmente concluído, o complexo Monarch poderá ultrapassar 8 gigawatts de capacidade elétrica bruta, conforme os documentos do IPO. Inicialmente, a Microsoft ocuparia parte das instalações. Em março, a companhia chegou a anunciar uma carta de intenções para participar do projeto. Entretanto, segundo a Bloomberg News, a Microsoft desistiu da instalação durante o verão do hemisfério norte. Com a decisão, a Anthropic ganhou espaço para ampliar sua presença no complexo. IPO da Nscale e a corrida por data centers O possível contrato de US$ 45 bilhões surge em um momento estratégico para a Nscale. A companhia prepara sua estreia na Bolsa e busca alcançar uma avaliação de mercado próxima de US$ 30 bilhões. Nesse cenário, um novo acordo bilionário poderia fortalecer o interesse dos investidores na oferta. Apesar disso, parte do mercado pressiona a empresa a reduzir sua expectativa de valuation, segundo informações anteriores da Bloomberg. Enquanto isso, a Anthropic amplia seus investimentos em infraestrutura para acompanhar o crescimento da demanda por inteligência artificial. A companhia já firmou outros contratos bilionários para garantir capacidade computacional. Entre eles, estão acordos de US$ 50 bilhões com a Fluidstack e US$ 10 bilhões com a startup Volta. Além disso, a empresa fechou um compromisso de US$ 45 bilhões com a SpaceX, de Elon Musk. Com esses investimentos, a Anthropic se tornou uma das principais responsáveis pelo avanço da demanda global por data centers voltados à IA. Em maio, o mercado avaliava a companhia em aproximadamente US$ 965 bilhões. Agora, a empresa também aparece entre as possíveis candidatas a realizar um IPO nos próximos meses. Caso avance com a abertura de capital, a operação poderá figurar entre as maiores ofertas recentes do setor de tecnologia. Ao mesmo tempo, a expansão acelerada da infraestrutura de IA aumenta a preocupação dos investidores com o endividamento das empresas. Afinal, a construção de data centers exige investimentos elevados, muitas vezes financiados por meio de empréstimos e emissão de títulos de dívida. Essa preocupação já afetou diferentes segmentos do mercado, desde ações de fabricantes de chips até títulos emitidos por empresas de computação em nuvem. Apesar desse cenário, a Nscale mantém seus planos de abertura de capital nos Estados Unidos. A companhia apresentou o pedido de listagem em setembro, mas ainda não iniciou a divulgação formal da oferta. Atualmente, a empresa busca responder aos questionamentos da Comissão de Valores Mobiliários dos Estados Unidos (SEC). Após concluir essa etapa, pretende iniciar o roadshow, período de apresentações aos potenciais investidores. Antes disso, em agosto, a Nscale levantou US$ 3,36 bilhões em uma rodada de investimentos pré-IPO. A operação teve a liderança da Third Point, gestora de Dan Loeb. A rodada também contou com aportes de Nvidia, Apollo Global Management, Citadel, Hudson Bay Capital e Abu Dhabi Investment Council.

artigo.texto: Huawei’s automotive technology company Yinwang has signed a strategic agreement with CATL and its battery-swapping subsidiary Contemporary Amperex Energy Service Technology, or CAES. The companies will work on battery compatibility, swapping networks and the integration of Huawei’s Qiankun driving technology with CATL’s Choco-Swap system. The partnership will connect vehicle, station and cloud services, allowing vehicles to determine when they need a battery swap, find a station, enter and align themselves, complete a 99-second automated swap, and drive away. Yinwang will also work with its automotive partners to develop vehicles compatible with CATL’s swapping network. The agreement was signed in Ningde, Fujian province, on October 19. artigo.texto: Paolla Oliveira beija Iza ao ser coroada rainha de bateria da Imperatriz Atriz e cantora se beijaram na boca e foram ovacionadas pelo público presente na quadra da agremiação Imperatriz Leopoldinense, no Rio de Janeiro Paolla Oliveira, 44, foi coroada rainha de bateria da escola carioca Imperatriz Leopoldinense na noite deste sábado (17) e ganhou um beijo na boca da cantora Iza, que estava com uma faixa de rainha da agremiação. As duas protagonizaram o momento íntimo e foram aplaudidas pelo público. A atriz foi recebida por uma festa dedicada às mulheres, que ressaltou o nome de várias componentes que "adotaram" o sobrenome Ramos, em referência ao bairro da Zona Norte do Rio de Janeiro. A nova rainha de bateria, que fez seu último desfile no Carnaval carioca como rainha da Grande Rio, em 2025, usava um look todo de pedrarias verdes, assim como a cantora Iza, que deixou o posto. As duas posaram juntas para as fotos e foi Iza quem colocou a faixa em Paolla. A atriz foi anunciada publicamente como nova rainha de bateria no dia 23 de setembro. Em comunicado divulgado à imprensa, Catia Drumond, presidente da Imperatriz, afirmou ter certeza de que Paolla chega para somar ao time e, principalmente, à comunidade de Ramos e toda a Zona da Leopoldina. "Que ela seja muito bem-vinda e, claro, muito feliz conosco." Após um ano longe da folia, Paolla agora volta para reinar diante dos ritmistas comandados pelo mestre Lolo. "O Carnaval vive em mim, vocês sabem. E a vida tem essa beleza do inesperado, em que a gente percebe que pode ainda ter muita coisa bonita para viver, sem nunca perder de vista tudo o que já foi vivido", disse ela à imprensa. "Estou muito feliz de estar aqui, de coração aberto e para começar mais uma história no carnaval. Chego com muito respeito, vontade de estar perto, conhecer, aprender e viver mais uma vez essa experiência rica e coletiva. Tem frio na barriga, claro, mas tem também uma alegria enorme por tudo que está começando", acrescentou. Com o enredo “A Memória do Rei e o Sumiço de Dona Júlia”, idealizado pelo carnavalesco Leandro Vieira, a Imperatriz Leopoldinense será a quarta escola a desfilar na Marquês de Sapucaí, fechando a segunda-feira de Carnaval, 8 de fevereiro, em busca do 10º título de sua história.

artigo.texto: Global clean energy brand BLUETTI showcased its portable power stations, residential energy storage systems, and commercial and industrial (C&I) energy solutions at the 140th Canton Fair, held from October 15 to 19, 2026. The exhibition highlighted the company’s products for personal, household, and business use while opening opportunities for partnerships with distributors and energy providers worldwide. The showcase covered solutions ranging from portable backup power to integrated solar, battery storage, and electric vehicle (EV) charging systems. BLUETTI also highlighted a pay-as-you-go financing model intended to make energy solutions more accessible to households and small businesses. Why it matters: Portable power and energy storage can help households and businesses manage power interruptions, while solar-powered systems offer another way to meet electricity needs. BLUETTI’s range of products also reflects the different requirements of individual users, residential customers, and commercial operations. The details: For portable power, BLUETTI presented its PREMIUM series, designed for outdoor activities, recreational vehicle travel, and home backup. It also showcased the Pioneer 5000, a professional portable power station rated for 5,000W of continuous output. The company said the Pioneer 5000 is designed for applications such as construction sites, equipment rental businesses, and agricultural operations. BLUETTI’s portable power solutions use lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) battery technology and support features such as fast charging, solar input, and uninterruptible power supply (UPS) protection. These features are intended to provide flexibility for users who need power in outdoor, residential, and professional settings. The bigger picture: BLUETTI also highlighted its HomeStar residential energy storage series, which supports AC and solar charging alongside app-based smart energy management. The company said these systems can serve households, clinics, and small businesses that need backup power. Another focus was BLUETTI’s integrated pay-as-you-go (PAYGO) solution, which uses flexible installment payments to make energy products more affordable. The BLUETTI GO platform supports digital operations management for the system. The company is inviting global partners to join its PAYGO solar network. Through platform integration, product deployment, and local distribution partnerships, BLUETTI aims to reach underserved households and micro-businesses, particularly in emerging markets. Between the lines: The PAYGO model is a key part of BLUETTI’s effort to expand beyond customers who can pay the full cost of an energy system upfront. Flexible payments may lower the initial financial barrier for eligible customers, while local distribution partners can help bring products to specific markets. However, the announcement does not provide detailed financing terms, eligibility requirements, or confirmed deployment plans for the Philippines. For businesses: BLUETTI’s commercial and industrial portfolio includes energy storage systems ranging from 64kWh to 240kWh, alongside integrated solar, storage, and EV charging solutions. The company said these systems can support peak shaving, energy arbitrage, backup power for critical loads, and flexible capacity expansion. By coordinating solar generation, battery storage, and EV charging demand, businesses may be able to manage peak electricity use, reduce reliance on the grid, and maintain operations during power disruptions. The potential benefits will depend on each installation’s energy demand, system configuration, local electricity rates, and operating conditions. What’s next: BLUETTI plans to strengthen its partnerships with distributors, energy developers, engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contractors, and other industry participants worldwide. The company aims to expand the deployment of its energy solutions across markets with different power requirements and business opportunities. BLUETTI reports serving more than 3.5 million customers worldwide and says it will continue developing products for personal, residential, and commercial applications. The Bottom Line: BLUETTI used the 140th Canton Fair to present its broader energy portfolio, from portable power stations and residential storage to large-scale commercial systems and PAYGO solar solutions. Its next steps focus on building global partnerships and expanding access to energy products for households and businesses. Get the latest from WALASTECH directly on your Google feed. artigo.texto: Dow Launches VOLTRICELL Platform to Advance Battery Innovation Dow Inc. DOW recently launched VOLTRICELL, a new battery cell materials platform designed to optimize battery manufacturing and improve performance. The platform expands Dow’s battery solutions portfolio and strengthens its presence in the industry. Dow, which is among the leading companies in the chemical space, along with DuPont de Nemours, Inc. DD, Eastman Chemical Company EMN and Air Products and Chemicals, Inc. APD, aims to bring together materials for electrodes, separators, coatings and battery cell packaging, including binders, dispersants, rheology modifiers, surfactants and specialty additives, through VOLTRICELL. These materials are designed to support higher energy density, longer cycle life, faster charging and scalable manufacturing. The platform integrates emerging technologies such as sodium-ion, silicon-anode and solid-state batteries. The new launch will be complemented by VORAFORCE TP1415 polyurethane resin for lightweight, flame-retardant composites, DOWSIL EF-6559 silicone foam for thermal management and electrical insulation, and DOWSIL FC-2024 coating for protecting battery housings and enclosures during thermal events. The introduction of VOLTRICELL supports growth by addressing manufacturers’ demand for materials that improve battery performance, safety and production scalability across the battery value chain. It builds on its deep materials science expertise and application development capabilities to foster innovation. For the second half of 2026, management plans to focus on growth and innovation in attractive end markets, investments to strengthen the portfolio and balanced capital allocation. Dow expects the growth and productivity benefits from Transform to Outperform to accelerate through the remainder of 2026 and into 2027. Dow expects approximately $200 million in additional benefits from Transform to Outperform during 2026. This raises the company’s expected total in-year benefits from self-help initiatives to more than $1.3 billion. Another industry leader, DuPont, raised the midpoint of its full-year 2026 operating EBITDA and adjusted earnings guidance. The company now expects net sales in the range of $7.16-$7.19 billion, operating EBITDA between $1.75 billion and $1.77 billion and adjusted earnings of $7.17-$7.32 per share. The outlook reflects continued strength across healthcare, industrial water and aerospace end markets. Management expects mid-single-digit organic sales growth in the second half and remains focused on productivity, profitable growth and shareholder value creation. Eastman, on its second-quarter call, said that it expects earnings to improve significantly from 2025. The company remains on track to deliver cost reductions of $125 million to $150 million, net of inflation. For the third quarter, adjusted earnings are projected to approach the second-quarter level of $1.97 per share. Advanced Materials EBIT is expected to increase on improved price-cost and asset utilization, while Fibers earnings should benefit from higher acetate tow purchases. Additives & Functional Products earnings are expected to decline modestly due to seasonal agriculture weakness, while Chemical Intermediates earnings are projected to ease as supply-chain disruptions lessen. Air Products, for fiscal 2026, raised its adjusted earnings guidance to $13.39-$13.49 per share from the prior range of $13-$13.25. artigo.texto: Siga Startups no Google Veja nossas notícias com mais destaque nas suas buscas. Siga Startups no Google Veja nossas notícias com mais destaque nas suas buscas. A falta de infraestrutura para energia elétrica está colocando obstáculos à expansão da inteligência artificial até mesmo em projetos que contam com grandes empresas de tecnologia. A Microsoft desistiu de um contrato para ser a principal cliente de um data center da Nscale em Loughton, no Reino Unido, depois que atrasos na conexão à rede elétrica empurraram a previsão de fornecimento de energia para 2030. O problema está na capacidade da infraestrutura elétrica de acompanhar o ritmo de expansão dos data centers. No Reino Unido, os pedidos de conexão à rede de transmissão para consumo de energia cresceram 460% nos seis meses até junho de 2025, segundo o governo britânico. Como resultado, alguns empreendimentos enfrentam esperas de até 15 anos para conseguir uma conexão à rede elétrica. O empreendimento estava previsto para entrar em operação no início de 2027. O plano era instalar 23.040 unidades de processamento gráfico (GPUs) GB300, da Nvidia, com capacidade computacional de 50 megawatts para apoiar os serviços de nuvem Azure da Microsoft no país. A decisão, porém, não significa o fim da parceria entre as duas empresas. Em comunicado à Reuters, a Microsoft afirmou que continua comprometida com a Nscale e com o desenvolvimento de infraestrutura digital. Segundo a companhia, a saída diz respeito exclusivamente ao local de Loughton. A Nscale também declarou que mantém uma relação de longo prazo com a Microsoft e que o problema não afeta seus outros contratos. A empresa afirmou que segue comprometida com o projeto e com o mercado britânico, enquanto avalia fontes alternativas de energia para viabilizar a operação. Infraestrutura computacional Fundada em Londres para fornecer infraestrutura voltada à inteligência artificial, a Nscale oferece capacidade computacional, data centers, energia e software para treinar e executar modelos de IA. A empresa, inclusive, entrou com um pedido de IPO nos Estados Unidos em setembro de 2026, com planos de listagem na New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) sob o ticker NSCL. A Nscale disputa esse mercado com empresas como CoreWeave, Nebius, Crusoe e Lambda Labs, que também fornecem infraestrutura computacional para aplicações de inteligência artificial. O episódio reforça que a expansão da IA depende não apenas da disponibilidade de chips e investimentos, mas também de condições físicas para operar os sistemas. Sem energia e conexões à rede elétrica no prazo necessário, projetos de grande porte podem sofrer atrasos ou perder contratos antes mesmo de entrar em funcionamento. Apesar do revés em Loughton, a Nscale segue atraindo investidores. Em 25 de setembro, a empresa anunciou a captação de US$ 3,36 bilhões por meio de notas conversíveis, que são empréstimos que podem virar ações da companhia no futuro. A rodada foi liderada pela Third Point e contou com a participação da Nvidia, que ainda se comprometeu a aportar mais US$ 1 bilhão em novembro. Segundo a Nscale, o dinheiro será usado para ampliar sua plataforma, que inclui desde usinas de energia próprias, instaladas junto ao local de consumo, até data centers e grandes clusters de GPUs. A Nscale também já deu o primeiro passo para abrir capital. A empresa protocolou recentemente seu pedido de IPO, com listagem prevista na Bolsa de Nova York (NYSE). O número de ações e a faixa de preço ainda não foram definidos. Siga Startups no Google Veja nossas notícias com mais destaque nas suas buscas. artigo.texto: Data center fervor is sweeping Central Florida, as voters pressure political leaders to keep the massive hubs of network infrastructure out of their cities and counties for fear they’ll gobble up local water resources and lead to higher electricity prices. And whether it’s in Florida’s governor race or local contests, candidates are being pinned down in forums and interviews for their positions on so-called hyper-scale data centers that polling shows voters loathe. A July University of North Florida poll found 68% of Florida voters disapprove of data centers being built in their area, including 84% of Democrats surveyed and 52% of Republicans. But perhaps most important in numerous races thought to be closely contested, 76% of voters with no party affiliation also don’t support them. Few people surveyed like data centers, the sprawling facilities that power artificial intelligence, among other things, said Sean Freeder, the director of the UNF Public Opinion Research Lab. “It’s the only question in the last several years in our polling where majorities dislike it across the board,” he said. “Democrats and independents are similar: They utterly hate them.” There are no hyper-scale centers in Central Florida, though a developer is marketing land in a rural section of Osceola County as a good site for one of the 5,000+ server facilities that are the focus of public ire. That’s prompted a petition urging county officials to turn down any such request should a data center developer try to buy the land. At least two other counties are considering moratoriums on data centers, even without any proposals in the pipeline. Data centers also have become one of the defining issues in the race to be Florida’s governor between Republican Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly, who have staked out significantly different positions on the issue. Donalds has offered some conditional support while Jolly, labeling his opponent “Data Center Donalds,” says he doesn’t want them in Florida. Complaints about the facilities range from how much water and electricity they consume to the constant noise of loud cooling fans measuring 100 decibels or more. Donalds has said he supports existing state law that allows cities and counties to determine for themselves whether or not to build data centers in their jurisdictions and says that utility rates cannot increase because of a hyperscale data center. He also has said he wants Florida to regulate how close such a facility can be to homes. After New York passed a one-year moratorium on large-scale centers, Donalds said that’s not the right approach for Florida. “But you also have to understand that when you start doing stuff like what New York just did, that’s a signal to the business community that this is not a place to invest capital,” he said. “This is not a place to invest in businesses, and so we have to be balanced and be mindful about that.” But the tech industry and data center developers have also been a major support of Donalds — with $6 million in direct donations and advertising support from donors such as utilities like Next Era and Duke Energy, as well as firms like Google and Meta, according to the state government watchdog website Seeking Rents. Jolly and Florida Democrats have tried to use the issue as they work to win the governor’s mansion for the first time in 30 years. After dubbing the Republican with the data center nickname, they use it frequently in online campaign ads. Jolly has said he would implement a one year moratorium on new data centers if elected. In an interview last month with the Orlando Sentinel, Jolly made his strategy clear: “Every time I open my mouth it’s ‘Housing, health care, education and no data centers,’” he said. “That’s it.” Florida Democrats this week hosted what they called the Data Center Donalds tour, stopping in downtown Orlando for a news conference. “Ultimately, data centers are not here to create new jobs; they’re here to exploit our resources, to impact our quality of life in a negative way and do it so that a handful of oligarchs can continue to be rich and wealthy while the rest of us struggle,” Rep. Anna Eskamani, D-Orlando, said. This comes as local governments across the state, including those dominated by Republicans, grapple with how to handle data center proposals. For instance, in conservative Lake County, last month the Board of County Commissioners enacted a 90-day pause on any new data centers. But the board this week asked its staff to draw up an ordinance that would allow them under a conditional use permit, which would mean any proposed center would require a vote by the commission. In Democrat-controlled Orange County, commissioners signaled last month they were likely to impose a moratorium on any new hyperscale data centers, though they haven’t yet voted to do so. Both candidates on the ballot next month for mayor, Tiffany Moore Russell, a Democrat, and Chris Messina, a Republican, have said they support a moratorium. Last month, several dozen speakers addressed commissioners urging them to support such restrictions. Toward the end of public comment, one resident, Angie Hatfield, made it plain. “As elected officials, if you don’t vote yes on a data moratorium, who are you representing?” she said. In Osceola, the commercial real estate firm CBRE is marketing 2,232 acres off Canoe Creek Road in Kenansville as “Florida’s premier hyperscale data center development site.” The listing notes it includes 1,066 buildable acres, with electrical service by Duke Energy and “significant water resources permitted.” The listing has drawn opposition in the form of a petition with more than 600 signatures. It urges Osceola County’s Board of County Commissioners to reject the project, if it comes forward. “They should reject the data center, and no vote should happen without public hearings and full disclosure of its water use, energy demands and environmental impact,” it reads. artigo.texto: Maharashtra State Power Generation Co. Ltd., Mumbai, India (MAHAGENCO) has issued a 500 MW/1,600 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) tender with two-hour and four-hour storage across Maharashtra. It envisions developing the project under a Build-Own-Operate (BOO) model, including Operation & Maintenance (O&M) for 15 years. It has sought online bids until November 5, 2026. It plans to develop six battery energy storage systems (BESS) totaling 500 MW/1,600 MWh. It includes developing 100 MW/400 MWh units each in Uran (Raigad district), Koradi, Nashik, and Khaperkheda. The tender also includes developing a 50 MW/100 MWh BESS project each at Chandrapur (Lakhmapur) and Parli, connected to MSETCL STU substations (33 kV and above). Each bidder must submit the bid processing fee of Rs. 10 lakh plus 18% GST for the total project capacity quoted via NEFT/RTGS to MAHAGENCO's account. The EMD (Earnest Money Deposit) or bid security for the project is Rs. 5 lakh/MW. Previous BESS Projects in Maharashtra Previously, companies such as Oriana Power Limited and GK Energy Limited won a combined Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) capacity of 1,050 MW / 2,100 MWh from MSEDCL. They secured this capacity under MSEDCL’s 2,000 MW / 4,000 MWh BESS tender, which was awarded within a month of its issuance. Oriana Power received two Letters of Award (LoAs) from MSEDCL to establish 900 MW / 1,800 MWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) in Maharashtra. Under these two LoAs, Oriana Power’s capacity is divided into 500 MW / 1,000 MWh and 400 MW / 800 MWh, respectively. GK Energy Limited also secured a BESS project after receiving a Letter of Award (LoA) from MSEDCL to set up a 150 MW / 300 MWh BESS project with Viability Gap Funding (VGF) support. Under this tender, the company was awarded the project at a tariff of Rs. 2,38,000/MW/month, resulting in an annual revenue of Rs. 42.84 crore (excluding GST) for 15 years from the commercial operation date (COD).

artigo.texto: Baker McKenzie Cairo advised Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited (“CATL”), one of the world’s largest and most innovative battery technology companies, on its cooperation with Battery Manufacturing Egypt (BME) (being a joint venture between Manufacturing Commercial Vehicles (MCV) and Auto D) for the establishment of a battery systems manufacturing plant in Egypt. Ghada El Ehwany, Managing Partner of Baker McKenzie Cairo, commented: “We are delighted to have supported CATL on this strategic project, which brings advanced battery technology and manufacturing capabilities to Egypt. The transaction reflects growing investment in the country’s industrial and clean technology sectors and demonstrates Egypt’s increasing role as a regional hub for advanced manufacturing and innovation.” Additionally, Zeinab Shohdy, M&A Counsel, commented: “This transaction called for a carefully tailored approach that balanced the parties’ commercial objectives while rigorously protecting CATL’s proprietary technology assets. We are proud to have helped establish a robust framework that enables CATL’s cutting-edge expertise and innovation to be deployed in Egypt while fully supporting its strategic business objectives.” Baker McKenzie acted as local counsel to CATL and advised on the structuring and implementation of the comprehensive contractual framework governing the parties’ technology cooperation, encompassing the commercialization of CATL’s advanced technology in Egypt while safeguarding its intellectual property rights and proprietary know-how. The scope of work included advising on the structuring and negotiation of the project agreements, navigating regulatory considerations across the transaction, and developing bespoke contractual protections designed to safeguard CATL’s long-term commercial interests. The Baker McKenzie Cairo team was led by the office’s Managing Partner Ghada El Ehwany, M&A Partner Hani Nassef, and Counsel Zeinab Shohdy, and further included Mohamed Elfar, Heba Samy, Omar Zaki and Mohamed El Baroudy. artigo.texto: 💻 A Anthropic, desenvolvedora do assistente de inteligência artificial Claude, está perto de ampliar ainda mais sua estrutura de computação. A Nscale, empresa de nuvem voltada à IA e apoiada pela Nvidia (NVDA), negocia a venda de capacidade computacional para a Anthropic em um acordo que pode chegar a cerca de US$ 45 bilhões, de acordo com pessoas a par das conversas. Acompanhe todas as notícias pelo celular! Baixe o app Se confirmado, este será o segundo grande contrato entre as duas empresas. Segundo documentos regulatórios ligados à oferta pública inicial planejada pela Nscale, a Anthropic já possui acordos de infraestrutura com a companhia que somam até aproximadamente US$ 44,6 bilhões. O negócio pode ser concluído nos próximos dias, segundo as fontes, que falaram sob condição de anonimato por se tratar de negociações privadas. As conversas seguem em andamento, os termos ainda podem mudar e nenhuma decisão definitiva foi tomada. Anthropic e Nscale não comentaram o assunto. Novo prédio terá 460 megawatts e chips Vera Rubin O novo contrato envolve uma instalação no complexo de data centers Monarch, que a Nscale desenvolve na Virgínia Ocidental, nos Estados Unidos. O segundo edifício do campus terá capacidade para entregar 460 megawatts de poder computacional e utilizará os chips de IA Vera Rubin, da Nvidia, a geração mais avançada da fabricante, segundo parte das fontes. Pelo desenho em discussão, a Anthropic também teria direito de preferência sobre um terceiro prédio previsto para o mesmo complexo. A dimensão do projeto ajuda a entender o interesse da empresa. De acordo com os documentos do IPO da Nscale, o campus Monarch poderá ultrapassar 8 gigawatts de capacidade elétrica bruta quando estiver totalmente concluído. Espaço foi aberto depois da desistência da Microsoft A entrada da Anthropic no complexo tem um antecedente curioso. Parte do campus Monarch seria inicialmente alugada pela Microsoft (MSFT), que em março havia anunciado a assinatura de uma carta de intenções para o projeto. No meio do ano, porém, a gigante de tecnologia desistiu da instalação, o que abriu espaço para que a Anthropic assumisse a operação. A Anthropic, uma das maiores clientes da Nscale, se transformou em um dos principais impulsionadores da demanda mundial por data centers dedicados à inteligência artificial. A empresa vem fechando uma série de acordos de grande porte para garantir capacidade computacional. Entre eles estão um contrato de US$ 50 bilhões com a Fluidstack, outro de US$ 10 bilhões com a startup de infraestrutura Volta e um acordo de US$ 45 bilhões com a SpaceX (SPCX), de Elon Musk. A busca por mais poder computacional acompanha o crescimento acelerado da companhia. Em julho, a Anthropic ultrapassou US$ 65 bilhões em receita anualizada, e em maio a empresa foi avaliada em US$ 965 bilhões. A desenvolvedora do Claude também é candidata a realizar sua própria abertura de capital nos próximos meses, em uma operação que pode estar entre as maiores da história recente do setor de tecnologia. Acordo pode reforçar o IPO da Nscale, avaliado em US$ 30 bi Do lado da Nscale, um novo contrato bilionário chega em um momento estratégico. A empresa busca uma avaliação de aproximadamente US$ 30 bilhões em seu IPO nos Estados Unidos, mas um grupo de investidores vem pressionando para que a companhia reduza essa meta de valuation. Um acordo dessa magnitude com um cliente como a Anthropic tende a fortalecer os argumentos da empresa diante do mercado. A Nscale protocolou o pedido público de listagem em setembro, mas ainda não iniciou formalmente a divulgação da oferta, embora o prazo regulatório de espera já tenha terminado. A empresa responde a questionamentos da SEC, órgão regulador do mercado de capitais americano, e pretende começar o roadshow com investidores assim que essas questões forem resolvidas. No mês passado, a companhia levantou US$ 3,36 bilhões em uma rodada pré-IPO liderada pela Third Point, de Dan Loeb, com participação de investidores como Nvidia, Apollo Global Management, Citadel, Hudson Bay Capital e Abu Dhabi Investment Council. 💰 O avanço dos investimentos em infraestrutura de IA, porém, vem acompanhado de cautela no mercado. Investidores têm demonstrado preocupação crescente com o volume de dívidas usado para financiar a expansão acelerada dos data centers, tema que tem pesado sobre ações de fabricantes de chips e sobre os títulos de dívida de empresas de computação em nuvem.

artigo.texto: With the Nov. 3 general election coming up, NHPR is sitting down with the candidates for governor to discuss top issues in the race and ask questions submitted by listeners and readers. Cinde Warmington, an attorney and former executive councilor from Concord, is the Democratic nominee. Here are some takeaways from her interview with NHPR. A full transcript of this conversation with All Things Considered host Julia Barnett follows below. On housing - Warmington said she would create a new state position of “housing czar” to focus on housing inventory and affordability. - She also promised investments in the Affordable Housing Fund, a state-administered loan program managed by New Hampshire Housing, to leverage federal funds. On data centers - Warmington is calling for an immediate moratorium on AI data centers in New Hampshire. She said the state needs to protect itself from skyrocketing electric rates and begin environmental impact studies as needed. On local or state agreements with ICE - “At the state level I do not believe that we should be cooperating with an organization that has been shown to be lawless, to be putting masked thugs on the street, terrorizing communities around our state.” On her past work as an opioid company lobbyist - Warmington said her representation of Purdue Pharma was 25 years ago. She said the pharmaceutical company lied to doctors and the FDA. - “I've been very, very clear that if I had known at the time what we all learned later, I would have had nothing, nothing to do with this work. And I certainly regret having anything to do with this work, knowing what we all know now.” What questions do you have about this year's elections? Let us know at voices@nhpr.org, and we could help you get the answers. Find all of our 2026 election coverage here. This transcript has been lightly edited for clarity. Rising housing costs continue to be a major issue for Granite Staters. As governor, what new ideas would you bring to address the housing crisis here? Well, as you said, housing costs are through the roof here. We've hit record highs under Kelly Ayotte's administration. I'm hearing about it everywhere I go across the state. Young people who can't afford to buy a home. Young people who can barely afford to pay rent. I'm hearing from seniors who are having trouble staying in their homes because of the skyrocketing property taxes, yet there's no place for them to downsize to. There's just no place for them to go. Small businesses, large businesses can't hire people because of the housing crisis in our state. This really needs to be taken head on. You may know that in our state, we actually have nobody accountable for knowing how many housing units we have, how many we need, and how we're going to get there. So first thing is, we're going to put in a housing czar who is going to be accountable for making sure we have a plan going forward. We're going to invest in the Affordable Housing Fund, because that's a fund where for every dollar we invest, we can leverage three federal dollars for that. We have been leaving millions of dollars on the table that should be invested in the Affordable Housing Fund, and we're going to fund that Housing Champions program, which was working so well. Almost half of our housing starts came from Housing Champions communities last year, and Kelly Ayotte defunded that program. There's so many more. We need to have all stakeholders at the table, but this is an all hands on deck problem that we need to tackle head on. And the state has struggled with a tight budget historically. Where would this money come from to support these efforts? This money was in the budget. And Kelly Ayotte decided to defund, for instance, the Housing Champions program. This is a matter of priorities and where you're going to put the priorities. Housing is a number one issue in the state, and it is going to affect not only the ability of people to stay here and raise their families here, but it affects the viability of our economy going forward. We absolutely have to be invested in this. As winter approaches, many folks are facing soaring fuel and electricity costs on top of other affordability concerns they may already have. What will you do as governor to help mitigate energy costs for Granite Staters, both in the short and long term? Well, I mean, first thing, we have to stand up and speak out about why energy costs are through the roof right now. As you mentioned, gas prices, heating oil prices are through the roof. That is largely because of Donald Trump's reckless war and his tariffs, both of things that Kelly Ayotte has simply refused to stand up and speak out about and defend Granite Staters. Also skyrocketing electric prices, up 15% since Kelly Ayotte came into office, due largely because of her failed energy policies that just are simply hostile towards energy efficiency and renewable energy. That's where we need to be putting the emphasis so that we have an energy policy for the future that will make sure we are bringing down electric rates and not also appointing people to our public utilities commission, who will continue to cater to the utilities. We need people on that commission that are looking out for our ratepayers. And when it comes to renewables, you've proposed getting to net-zero emissions by 2040. That's 14 years away. How realistic is that? Well, I proposed 2040 in the last election, and that is when we had sort of record investments by the federal government in helping communities to do that. Under the Trump administration, of course, that money has gone away. So they've made the 2040 date impossible. But there needs to be a date out there somewhere where we are decreasing our dependence on fossil fuels. I do want to clear up a misunderstanding or a misrepresentation of my position. I am not against all emissions. I'm not against gas-powered cars. I am not against gas stoves. I cook with a gas stove myself. And net zero does not mean zero.

artigo.texto: District 12 Senator Amy Sinclair Earlier this month, it was announced that a $15 billion deal was in the works to bring a steel mill to Iowa. Iowa Senator for District 12 Amy Sinclair says that many are looking at the deal positively, while some other have also questioned it, asking what the difference is between this deal, and that of data centers. She tells Raccoon Valley Radio what that difference is. “I will say there’s some conversation surrounding data centers and how those are going in. The use of tax dollars for those, the use of water. There are some real concerns and some issues that I think will arise in the coming session to have a real honest conversation about how much farmland they’re taking up, about how many jobs they’re actually producing, about whether or not tax incentives at all should go into those data centers, given the fact that they’re owned by multi-billion dollar organizations that would be building data centers regardless.” Sinclair mentions that additionally, while this steel mill deal would qualify for megasite incentives under Iowa law, data centers do not. She adds that many incentives that go towards data centers are actually from local governments instead of the state.

artigo.texto: A China está a intensificar os investimentos no armazenamento de energia e na conservação dos ecossistemas, procurando conciliar a transição energética com a proteção ambiental. As duas prioridades foram destacadas em iniciativas divulgadas pela agência estatal Xinhua. Durante a Conferência Mundial de Armazenamento de Energia, realizada em Ningde, foram apresentados dados que atribuem à China 56% da expansão mundial da capacidade de armazenamento em baterias em 2025. No primeiro semestre de 2026, a produção chinesa de baterias destinadas a este setor ultrapassou 420 GWh, mais 110% do que no período homólogo. Paralelamente, o Presidente Xi Jinping defendeu o reforço da conservação ecológica durante uma visita à Mongólia Interior. Na reserva natural do lago Huangqihai, destacou a importância da recuperação das zonas húmidas, da proteção da biodiversidade e do cumprimento da legislação ambiental. A estratégia inclui ainda novas inspeções ambientais e a aplicação do Código Ecológico e Ambiental, em vigor desde agosto. Apesar dos progressos anunciados, persistem desafios relacionados com os custos das tecnologias, a fiscalização e a sustentabilidade dos resultados a longo prazo.

artigo.texto: Pro-Russian accounts targeting Ukrainians on Facebook and Telegram sharply declined after Ukrainian drone strikes on Yandex data centers, according to a new report from a Ukrainian government agency. It’s the most direct evidence so far behind a claim that went viral last week, but it falls well short of proving it. The report comes from Ukraine’s Center for Countering Disinformation (CCD), which operates under the country’s National Security and Defense Council. It was published Oct. 15, and United24 Media covered it on Oct. 17. The CCD used software from the Ukrainian security firm Osavul to track accounts it flagged as showing "signs of inauthentic behavior." According to Osavul's website, the firm "builds AI-powered risk intelligence for hybrid threats." According to United24, the CCD analyzed 22,664 messages from 5,201 accounts posted between Oct. 6 and 12, across 26 topics in Ukraine’s information space. The report found two sharp drops in activity, each following a strike that fully shut down a Yandex facility. On Oct. 8, the day a fire took Yandex’s data center in Sasovo, in Russia’s Ryazan region, offline, messages fell 83.6 percent, from 4,032 to 660. The number of active accounts fell by a similar share. Activity rebounded past pre-strike levels by Oct. 10, but on Oct. 12, a day after a strike fully halted operations at a Yandex data center in Vladimir, messages fell by 42.6 percent and active accounts dropped by 41 percent. A smaller group of 98 accounts that posted pro-war propaganda, conspiracy theories, or calls for violence followed the same pattern. The CCD concluded that strikes on data centers can significantly disrupt Russian influence networks, but the effect appears to be short-lived. Mashable was unable to verify the CCD’s findings independently. Before publication, we emailed Osavul to request the underlying dataset, the criteria it uses to flag inauthentic behavior, and any information about where the accounts were hosted. Osavul did not respond by publication time. The report never defines "inauthentic behavior." While the term is quite broad, some general signals that researchers typically attribute to bot accounts include newly created profiles, unusually high posting volume, blank or AI-generated profile photos, and activity across many unrelated political narratives. Without Osavul’s criteria, it’s unclear whether these accounts are automated, run by coordinated humans, or a mix of both. Still, if the numbers hold up, they point to something real. The CCD argues that the drops show strikes on data centers can significantly constrain Russia’s information operations by disrupting the automated networks behind them. However, the agency also acknowledges how quickly the accounts came back, suggesting the disruptions were "substantial but short-lived." Why it matters The findings arrive after a week of overheated claims. Last week, Mashable looked at viral claims that Ukrainian drone strikes on Yandex data centers had knocked Russia’s bot army offline. The conclusion we and other outlets reached was that the data behind those claims couldn’t support them. That claim spread like wildfire on social media, amplified by European officials and even backed up by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Speaking at the Warsaw Security Forum, President Zelenskyy said "everyone noticed" a drop in Russian bot activity. Social media users echoed similar observations about the seemingly stark decline in pro-GOP and pro-AfD posts after the strikes. It was an easy idea to believe, given how platforms like Facebook and X incentivize and reward polarizing political ragebait, and Russia’s online influence operations are well-documented. The claim also seemed to have supporting data. United24 Media, the Ukrainian government-run outlet whose reporting drove much of the conversation, cited an analysis by The Deep Dive of Cloudflare Radar data. That data showed automated traffic from Yandex’s network had nearly vanished by Oct. 11. As Mashable reported at the time, that data couldn’t support the claim. "Automated traffic" means any request that software, rather than a person, sends to a website, and most of it is mundane. Yandex, often called "Russia's Google," runs the Federation's biggest search engine, so its network constantly sends out crawlers to index the web. Knocking its data centers offline would stop that traffic, whether or not a single troll account went quiet. We found no published evidence tying influence campaigns on social media to Yandex servers, and United24 acknowledged the same limitation. Cloudflare has since published its own analysis. It said its data doesn’t appear to support claims that the strikes crippled social media manipulation, though it couldn’t rule out a connection. Zelenskyy’s office has also narrowed his remarks. According to BBC Verify, his office said the president was "talking about the atmosphere on social media" rather than a fall in bot activity.

artigo.texto: Conciliar a produção agrícola com a conservação das florestas, ampliar a restauração de áreas degradadas e transformar a preservação ambiental em oportunidades econômicas estão entre os desafios e as possibilidades para o Pará. Em entrevista ao Grupo Liberal, Leonardo Sobral, diretor de Florestas e Restauração do Imaflora (Instituto de Manejo e Certificação Florestal e Agrícola), destaca o potencial do estado para avançar nessa agenda por meio de incentivos econômicos, do mercado de carbono, da bioeconomia e das concessões florestais para restauração. O especialista também ressalta a importância de valorizar os produtos da floresta em pé e de fortalecer iniciativas que conciliem conservação ambiental, produção sustentável e geração de renda. 1.Quais são hoje os maiores desafios para conciliar a produção agrícola com a conservação das florestas no estado do Pará? A primeira grande notícia é que a conciliação da produção agrícola com a área florestal é totalmente possível. Hoje não só no estado do Pará, mas em toda a Amazônia, existem áreas produtivas, áreas com aptidão de produção agrícola e que elas devem cada vez mais implementar as boas práticas produtivas. Nesse caso, eu me refiro a boas práticas tanto do ponto de vista ambiental como do ponto de vista social. E, ao mesmo tempo, mantendo a sua reserva florestal, mantendo a floresta em pé, sem que haja essa concorrência, vamos dizer, entre as atividades. 2. Como o Imaflora avalia o ritmo atual das iniciativas de reflorestamento e restauração na Amazônia? Estamos avançando no tempo necessário ou ainda não? O tema da restauração florestal no ambiente de pesquisa já é muito consolidado, e nos últimos anos, a gente viu um grande interesse do setor privado, principalmente dada a questão do carbono florestal. A gente tem que entender que a restauração florestal é uma forma de, ao mesmo tempo que você planta as árvores, está restaurando a floresta original, e, ao crescer as árvores, ela faz o sequestro do carbono, a remoção do carbono. Você consegue dessa forma estabelecer um projeto de carbono e ter uma remuneração por esse carbono que está sendo retirado da atmosfera. Nos últimos anos, essa atividade vem crescendo bastante, vem ganhando muita importância no Brasil, no estado do Pará, mas como você pergunta do ritmo, tem muito ainda o que se fazer. O que a gente vem discutindo é que cada vez mais deva ter incentivos econômicos. Além do carbono, outros produtos, seja madeira, seja produtos não madeireiros, possam vir atrelados a essa atividade, para que ela seja viável cada vez mais do ponto de vista econômico mesmo. Ainda tem um longo caminho a ser percorrido, mas o que a gente vem vendo atualmente são muitas ações de fortalecimento desse setor. A gente entende que o estado do Pará tem aptidão para isso. Ele tem muitas áreas degradadas que poderiam estar sendo restauradas e já tem um programa de governo instituído, então digo que hoje temos um ambiente favorável para avançar na agenda de restauração. 3.O Imaflora tem algum projeto que avalia como destaque, com importância nessa questão do carbono no Pará ou na Amazônia? A gente tem uma plataforma de monitoramento chamada “Carbon Track”. Essa plataforma de monitoramento da restauração florestal avalia a qualidade da restauração e ao mesmo tempo faz uma avaliação da quantidade de carbono que está sendo sequestrado. Hoje existem diversas tecnologias nesse mundo de avanço tecnológico. Tem muita informação. Tem muita novidade. Por exemplo, a gente fez o monitoramento de uma área utilizando tecnologia de LiDAR (sigla para Light Detection and Ranging, ou Detecção e Alcance de Luz), que são lasers, embarcados num drone. Isso reduz o tempo de monitoramento em campo, otimizando essa atividade e trazendo maior precisão para a quantificação de carbono. Esse é só um exemplo. Tem outras tecnologias existentes e a gente vem cada vez mais também avançando nessa atividade. 4.Belém e o Pará estão no centro das atenções globais devido à agenda climática, principalmente depois da Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Mudanças Climáticas (COP 30) que ocorreu em novembro de 2025 aqui. Como a população local pode se beneficiar diretamente da chamada bioeconomia? Belém de fato está no centro da atenção climática, depois da COP 30. A cidade conseguiu de fato fazer uma COP muito bem feita, no meu ponto de vista, e eu acho que a partir daí muitos benefícios podem advir disso. A bioeconomia é um exemplo. Quando a gente fala de bioeconomia, a gente está falando de produtos da floresta, produtos da sociobioeconomia, que vão desde frutos, óleos, sementes. É uma gama enorme de produtos. A COP trouxe um legado importante: um olhar também internacional. As pessoas de vários países tiveram em Belém, podendo ver a riqueza e valorizar esses produtos. Nem o próprio Brasil também conhece essa riqueza e valoriza esses produtos. Acho que nessa perspectiva de valorização do produto, que é um produto que vai para a culinária, por exemplo, é super importante que eles sejam valorizados e reconhecidos. Por quê? Porque quanto mais a gente valoriza produtos da floresta, mais incentivo a gente está dando para que a floresta permaneça em pé. Então, conectando um pouco os produtos da sociobioeconomia com a questão climática, a questão de contenção do desmatamento, a premissa é essa - a gente precisa valorizar a floresta em pé através de seus produtos e de seus serviços que são prestados não só localmente, no estado do Pará, em Belém, mas para todo mundo. É a regulação do clima que a gente está falando. 5. Na prática, de que forma a certificação florestal ajuda a combater o desmatamento ilegal na Amazônia? artigo.texto: The Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission (GERC) has finalized the Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission (Grid Interactive Battery Energy Storage System) Regulations, 2026, establishing a regulatory framework for integrating Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) into Gujarat’s electricity grid. The regulations aim to improve grid stability, enhance operational flexibility, and support the growing integration of renewable energy sources, particularly solar and wind power, whose generation depends on weather conditions. The new framework aligns with guidelines issued by the Ministry of Power, Government of India, which recognize energy storage as an important component of electricity generation, transmission, distribution, and ancillary services. Battery energy storage systems can help balance electricity supply and demand by storing surplus power and releasing it when required, thereby supporting reliable grid operations. GERC initiated the regulatory process by publishing the draft regulations on May 12, 2026. The Commission subsequently conducted a public consultation process to gather feedback from stakeholders. Written comments and objections were received from 20 stakeholders, followed by a public hearing on June 15, 2026. The finalized regulations incorporate the Commission’s decisions on key aspects of BESS procurement, project registration, operating models, charging arrangements, and grid control. Under the finalized framework, electricity distribution licensees and other applicable licensees are primarily required to procure BESS capacity through competitive bidding under Section 63 of the Electricity Act, 2003. This approach is intended to promote transparent procurement and cost-effective tariff discovery. Procurement under Section 62 will be permitted only in exceptional circumstances, subject to prior approval from the Commission and the submission of adequate techno-commercial justification. The regulations also establish registration and minimum project-size requirements for grid-connected battery storage installations in Gujarat. All grid-connected BESS projects must register with the Gujarat Energy Development Agency (GEDA). For standalone installations, the minimum individual project size has been specified as above 1 MW in power capacity, with an energy storage duration of at least two hours. Such projects must connect to the electricity network at 11 kV or higher. The framework allows battery storage systems to operate under different business models, including co-located projects alongside renewable energy plants, standalone installations, systems embedded within transmission or distribution networks, and consumer or prosumer arrangements. These provisions are intended to accommodate different applications of energy storage across the power sector. For co-located BESS installations, the Commission has specified that charging must take place exclusively from the associated renewable energy plant. This restriction is designed to avoid complications in energy accounting and Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) compliance. Grid charging without the appropriate contract demand will attract temporary supply tariffs, discouraging unauthorized electricity consumption through the grid. The regulations also clarify the role of the State Load Despatch Centre (SLDC) in maintaining grid security. The SLDC will retain overriding authority to issue dispatch instructions to all grid-connected BESS during grid disturbances, helping safeguard system reliability. With these regulations, Gujarat has established a framework for the controlled deployment and operation of battery energy storage systems. The measures are expected to support renewable energy integration, improve grid flexibility, and strengthen the state’s ability to manage changing electricity demand and generation patterns. artigo.texto: The Converter as the Control Point for AI Data Center Power With AI workloads driving unprecedented growth in data center power demand, projected by some analysts to reach as much as 70% annually through 2027, the industry's first AI power debate centered on capacity: where will the next hundreds of megawatts come from? AI factories introduce concentrated, fast-changing loads that can create steep ramps in demand and power consumption. At the same time, utilities and grid operators are scrutinizing how very large loads behave during disturbances, not simply whether enough generation exists to serve them. This creates a new design requirement. The data center must remain highly available while presenting the grid, on-site generators, and internal distribution system with a manageable load profile. The solution is a coordinated power architecture in which converters, storage, controls, protection, medium-voltage equipment, and digital systems work as one. Within that architecture, PCS has become increasingly important. As AI facilities grow in scale and complexity, they are evolving from simple power electronics components into key control layers that help coordinate how energy moves through the site. No longer just a conversion device In a conventional description, a converter does what it says: converts direct current from a battery or renewable source into alternating current for the facility or grid and reverses that flow when charging storage. In an AI data center, a modern PCS functions as a high-speed, controllable electrical interface, regulating active and reactive power, limiting current, shaping ramp rates, supporting voltage and frequency stability, and responding through grid-connected and islanded operating modes. That distinction matters because AI power problems happen on several timescales. Fast converter controls can respond to sharp electrical changes, battery energy storage systems (BESS) can buffer sustained ramps or temporary capacity limits, and Power Plant Controllers (PPC) can coordinate the PCS with generators, utility signals, switchgear, facility-management systems, and state-of-charge constraints. Together, these layers help make volatile loads more predictable. Four roles for power conversion in the AI power architecture 1. Load smoothing and generator protection AI workload changes can push on-site generation and utility connections beyond comfortable ramp-rate or power-quality envelopes. A bidirectional PCS paired with BESS can absorb excess power or inject power rapidly, reducing sudden changes seen by the rest of the system. 2. Voltage support and disturbance ride-through Converters can supply or absorb reactive power and follow a defined ride-through behavior. The objective is to prevent a short grid event from becoming a large, coordinated loss of data center load or a site-wide transfer event. 3. Grid-connected, islanded, and restoration modes With appropriate system design, controls, and protection, storage and PCS can support transitions between grid-connected and islanded operation, stabilize an islanded bus, and contribute to restoration or black-start pathways. These are system functions and must be validated at the site level. 4. Capacity shaping and flexible interconnection When a grid connection is constrained, storage can reduce peaks, manage import limits, and help the facility operate within an agreed envelope. This does not eliminate the need for interconnection studies or network upgrades, but it can create additional design options. A practical architecture For large campuses, PCS should be evaluated as part of a repeatable medium-voltage building block rather than as an isolated converter. A typical architecture can combine battery blocks, medium-voltage transformers, switchgear, power plant controllers, protection, telemetry, and supervisory controls. Modular, factory-tested blocks reduce the number of site interfaces and create a platform that can be repeated as the campus expands, reducing integration risks and streamlining deployment. The control hierarchy is equally important. Converter-level controls provide the fastest response. Plant controls coordinate multiple converters and enforce site-level active-power, reactive-power, voltage, frequency, and import or export objectives. Higher-level energy management can optimize state of charge, demand response, market participation, and on-site generation use. Clear ownership of each control loop is essential to avoid conflicting commands or unstable interactions. Model first, then prove the response AI data centers require a validation process that connects product capability to site behavior. The work should begin with the actual load profile, grid strength, fault levels, generator characteristics, protection philosophy, and intended operating modes. Steady-state studies alone are not enough for the most dynamic use cases. Electromagnetic-transient models, hardware-in-the-loop testing and staged commissioning can be used to test ramp events, voltage disturbances, current limits, control handoffs, and islanding sequences before the full site is energized. This model-to-test-to-commission approach also changes procurement. Instead of buying an inverter only against a nameplate rating, owners can define measurable performance at the point of interconnection: response time, ramp-rate control, reactive capability, recovery after a fault, operating envelopes, and telemetry. The commercial specification becomes a performance specification. From passive load to grid-interacting energy system The power challenge facing AI data centers is not solved by adding capacity alone. It is solved by coordinating capacity with controllability. As campuses combine utility connections, on-site generation, batteries, renewables, and increasingly power-dense compute, the converter becomes one of the few assets capable of acting fast enough to keep those elements working together. artigo.texto: Residents in four Madison County townships will vote in November on an advisory measure asking whether data center development should be allowed in their communities. Ballot initiatives in Chouteau, Granite City, Nameoki and Venice townships will ask voters whether they support future data center development and construction. In Illinois, townships are subdivisions of local government that operate alongside cities and villages. The township’s elected board may oversee local infrastructure, such as water and sewer services. Each of the townships included in the advisory measure overlaps with Granite City. Because the measures are nonbinding, they would not ban data centers even if residents vote against the projects. Heather Groetecke, a lifelong Granite City resident, led the effort to collect signatures for the initiatives. She first became aware of potential data center development near her home in Nameoki Township when officials held community meetings this spring about proposals for two sites in Granite City and another in nearby Pontoon Beach. Groetecke said she began organizing when officials failed to answer her questions about environmental hazards and other concerns. “I (have) never really even been involved in politics in my whole life, and I don’t really like it either,” she said. “But I don’t want a data center.” Groetecke initially wanted to put a data center moratorium on the ballot. But she said political advisers close to the signature campaign recommended a nonbinding measure because it would be easier to pass. “They can still do what they want to do,” Groetecke said. “But if we win by the majority, I think that speaks volumes.” Data center proposals in the Granite City area Data center developers are eyeing the Granite City area for projects. City officials heard public comment about a proposal involving two sites along the Route 3 industrial corridor. Officials in nearby Pontoon Beach heard a similar proposal in May, the Alton Telegraph reported. The Belleville News-Democrat reported that the Granite City project received mixed reviews in a February forum. Trade union leaders voiced support for the potential economic development and property tax revenue, while other residents said they were concerned about utility rate hikes, environmental impacts and transparency. Developer Cloverleaf Infrastructure said in a public city council meeting in Granite City last November that it doesn’t sign nondisclosure agreements with local governments. The developer also promised not to use groundwater wells to cool its data centers and suggested “enforceable” zoning requirements to limit noise and light pollution. Cloverleaf officials have said the company works with big names in tech, including Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Google and OpenAI. Some residents accused Granite City Mayor Mike Parkinson and other city officials of misleading the public when they said that they knew little about data center development in public meetings. Residents said in May that officials negotiated a possible land sale for a data center project with special governing district America’s Central Port before alerting the public. Parkinson told the Belleville News-Democrat that the documents cited by residents were taken out of context and that the city never collaborated with the port authority to bring in data center projects. Months before the community meetings, Parkinson, Madison County Executive Chris Slusser and Granite City’s economic development director, Cathy Hamilton, were among several St. Louis-area leaders who toured a Google data center on a trip financed by Greater St. Louis Inc. Officials were asked to sign nondisclosure agreements before touring the facility. Granite City officials say the data center project was tabled along with similar proposals in Edwardsville and Troy, Illinois. Granite City officials did not respond to requests for comment.

artigo.texto: Transmission grid fees in Belgium could increase by 92% for battery energy storage systems (BESS) and by 150% for offshore wind projects by 2035, according to a study by Aurora Energy Research examining the evolution of network tariffs and their economic implications for energy projects. The report, titled Transmission Grid Fees in Belgium: Outlook & Impact Assessment, was commissioned by Adaptogen Capital, BayWa r.e., Norther, Otary and Storm, amid regulatory changes affecting the costs of accessing and using Belgium's electricity transmission infrastructure. The analysis follows the publication of the tariff methodology for the 2028–2031 regulatory period by Belgium's energy regulator, CREG, ahead of transmission system operator Elia's expected publication of updated grid tariffs in 2027. Grid fees for batteries could reach €112/kW by 2035 One of the main changes examined in the study is the planned phase-out of the 10-year grid fee exemption for battery energy storage systems, a mechanism that has helped limit network costs for eligible storage projects. According to Aurora's central scenario, the combined effect of removing this exemption and rising overall network costs could result in a 92% increase in the total grid fee burden for a typical battery, reaching €112/kW by 2035. The study estimates that, without mitigation measures, average annual margins for battery storage projects could fall to €47/kW. Björn Hofman, Senior Associate, Advisory, at Aurora Energy Research, warned that rising grid fees could place additional pressure on the economics of battery storage projects and other grid-connected assets in Belgium. He noted that discount mechanisms are available, including incentives to avoid charging during peak hours and the potential introduction of voluntary flexible connection agreements. However, these measures are unlikely to fully offset the projected increase in network costs. Offshore wind faces a potential 150% increase The second major regulatory change identified by Aurora is the introduction of a capacity-based feed-in fee for electricity injected into the grid, which would add another cost component for renewable electricity generators. According to the analysis, Belgium's projected feed-in fees could reach €11/kW, exceeding the levels expected in neighbouring markets. Germany is preparing similar charges in the range of €4–7/kW, while Belgium has yet to announce comparable protections for existing projects or developments that have already committed investment. Aurora notes that Germany has announced a 20-year exemption for assets that reach a final investment decision (FID) before the new fee enters into force. The Netherlands is also expected to introduce an equivalent exemption to maintain comparable investment conditions across European markets. Belgium, by contrast, has not yet made a similar commitment to protect projects from changes to the tariff framework after investment decisions have been taken. This regulatory difference could affect the competitiveness of Belgian renewable energy projects relative to those in neighbouring countries. Industry representatives call for protection of existing investments Mathias Verkest, CEO of Otary, warned that allocating grid costs between electricity consumers and producers could have implications for final electricity prices and the financing conditions of new projects. He explained that developers may seek to pass additional costs on to consumers. Where this is not possible, higher network charges could instead translate into increased risk premiums, potentially raising the cost of financing new developments. Verkest therefore supported the introduction of grandfathering provisions to protect existing and upcoming projects, following the approach adopted in Germany and the Netherlands. Similarly, Christophe De Schryver, Executive Manager at Norther, stressed that investment in renewable electricity generation depends on a stable and predictable regulatory framework over long periods. He warned that introducing substantial new injection charges without protecting previously committed investments could undermine investor confidence and weaken Belgium's attractiveness for future energy investment. Aurora identifies measures to limit rising network costs The study outlines several measures that could help contain the increase in transmission charges, including alternative financing arrangements for part of the required grid investment, stimulating electricity demand to expand the tariff billing base, and stricter cost controls. For the remaining costs, Aurora recommends implementing grandfathering exemptions for existing and upcoming projects, maintaining discounts for avoiding consumption during peak periods, and extending flexible connection discounts to both voluntary and imposed agreements. The consultancy warns that, without regulatory action, higher network charges could delay investment decisions in storage and renewable electricity generation while increasing costs for electricity consumers. The report therefore identifies the evolution of transmission tariffs as a factor that could influence the profitability of BESS and offshore wind projects, financing conditions and the deployment of renewable energy capacity in Belgium over the coming decade.

artigo.texto: As Diwali approaches and Delhi braces for its annual smog season, conversations about air quality usually turn to firecrackers and stubble burning. These conversations seem to miss out on pollution caused by factories, power plants and furnaces that run all year and are a steadier source of pollution. This is a fitting moment to ask what India’s biggest industrial emitters have been doing, and how the 2026 UN Climate Change COP31 will bring about an environmental change for the better. Starting November, for the first time, Indian factories will be able to buy and sell carbon credit certificates on power exchanges, finally turning a carbon credit trading scheme which was notified by the government in 2023, into a working market reality. The legal foundation for the concept is the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2022, which empowered the government to create an Indian carbon market and a carbon credit trading scheme which was notified in 2023. The Bureau of Energy Efficiency has issued emission targets to around 490 industrial units across seven sectors and credits are expected to be issued this month, with trading between November and January. To understand this better how the carbon credit market works, think back to school. Imagine a school where every student gets a fixed number of late passes each term. The punctual kids end up with spares and the chronic latecomers run short. Now let them trade. The early birds sell their extras, the sleepyheads buy them, and the school still meets its overall punctuality target. Replace late passes with tonnes of carbon dioxide and students with factories, and what you have is carbon credit trading. The idea is simple. A government sets emission targets for polluting industries. A company that beats its target earns certain credits, one for every tonne of carbon dioxide it avoided. A company that misses must buy credits from the one who met its targets. Therefore, pollution gets a price tag, and environment friendly industry practices becomes a way of earning money instead of a cost. While the efficacy of the scheme, and the volume of trade it inspires, remains to be seen, there are interesting aspects of the scheme which deserve to be highlighted. Firstly, the credit trading scheme operates differently from other types of environment policies. For instance a green tax, such as a carbon tax or India’s former coal cess, puts a fixed price on pollution. Every company pays for every tonne it emits, and the money goes to the government. As opposed to this, the carbon credit trading scheme would target the emissions more directly leading to actual reduction while letting the market set the price for per unit emission. Secondly, the scheme has a dual benefit: it cuts pollution while putting money in motion, since companies that clean up earn credits to sell their certificates. One market research firm valued India’s carbon credit market at about 34 billion dollars in 2025 and expects it to grow more than tenfold by 2034. The scheme also helps India keep its promises under the Paris Agreement, where it has pledged to cut the emissions intensity of its economy by 47 percent by 2035. Lastly, the scheme sets targets as emissions per unit of output rather than as a cap on total emissions per industry. That choice matters for a developing country like India, where industry must keep expanding to support growth and jobs. An intensity-based approach lets factories grow while still rewarding them for producing more cleanly. It does, however, raise two concerns. The first is a practical one: since industries would expand and output would rise even if per unit emissions becomes cleaner, India’s total emissions may still continue to climb in the long run. The second concern is more fundamental: the scheme risks becoming a permission slip to pollute, letting heavy emitters buy their way out of their obligations instead of changing how they operate. So is this a climate tool or an accounting trick? The answer would depend upon its enforcement. A carbon market with tough targets, honest verification and real penalties would ultimately make clean factories richer. While lasting positive impact on climate would require cleaner technology, stronger enforcement and steady shifts in how industry operates, the carbon credit scheme is a meaningful first step in that direction because it would incentivise industries to invest in developing cleaner technologies with the aim of long term monetary gains. Nakul Dewan is a Senior Advocate and King’s Counsel.

artigo.texto: A preservação de florestas e a recuperação de áreas degradadas podem gerar créditos de carbono e abrir oportunidades econômicas na Amazônia. Em entrevista ao Grupo Liberal, Leonardo Sobral, diretor de Florestas e Restauração do Imaflora (Instituto de Manejo e Certificação Florestal e Agrícola), explica como funciona esse mecanismo, que busca valorizar a manutenção da floresta em pé e incentivar a restauração florestal. Segundo o especialista, as árvores armazenam carbono em sua estrutura, e a quantidade presente em uma área pode ser calculada a partir da medição da vegetação. Como exemplo, ele cita que um hectare de floresta pode armazenar cerca de 300 toneladas de carbono. “À medida que você evita que essa floresta seja derrubada, seja desmatada, eu posso, através de um projeto, vender esse carbono”, explica Sobral. VEJA MAIS Nesse caso, a quantidade de carbono cuja emissão foi evitada pode gerar créditos comercializados no mercado. O mecanismo também pode ser aplicado à recuperação de áreas degradadas. Quando árvores são plantadas durante um projeto de restauração florestal, elas absorvem carbono da atmosfera, permitindo calcular a quantidade de créditos gerados. “Essa restauração, quando planta as árvores, sequestra carbono. Com essa quantidade de carbono que é sequestrado é feito todo esse cálculo para ver quantos créditos de carbono estão sendo gerados”, afirma o diretor do Imaflora.
